summary: GitHub observer REST validators survive daemon restarts, isolate credentials, and log HTTP budget evidence; secondary limits honor Retry-After instead of waiting for the primary reset.

replay.detail: Existing observations and polling intervals are unchanged. A 304 reuses the complete cached response without a new changed observation.

schema.detail: No claim-store schema change. The configured state directory keeps private github-http-cache response bodies, ETags, Last-Modified values and pagination links, keyed by URL and credential identity.

rules.detail: A 403 or 429 with Retry-After or nonzero primary remaining budget is treated as a secondary limit. Retry-After is honored; otherwise secondary limits wait at least one minute. Only an exhausted primary budget uses x-ratelimit-reset.

compatibility.detail: Observer refusal claims retain HTTP status, resource, remaining and retry-after in the existing reason field; the closed claim schema is unchanged. Rust GitHub HTTP calls append the agent gh wrapper JSONL envelope plus method, path, status, remaining, resource, retry_after and not_modified to AGENT_POLICY_STATE_DIR/gh-usage.jsonl, defaulting to HOME/.local/state/agent-policy/gh-usage.jsonl. Missing response fields are null; credentials and request bodies are never logged.

downtime.detail: Restart revalidates stored bodies conditionally rather than trusting their freshness.

recovery.detail: Removing github-http-cache safely causes full authenticated reads on the next polls. Rollback ignores the cache and additional response evidence.
